\section[el conocimiento]{el conocimiento — the knowledge}

\label{lesson:ES-C598-conocimiento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to assess, then the Spanish for the assessment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el conocimiento}
\textbf{el conocimiento} — \textquotedblleft{}the knowledge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tiene buenos conocimientos de inglés.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She has a good knowledge of English.}
\end{quote}

In the plural it means what you know about a subject.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{conocimiento} is built on \emph{conocer}, inherited from Latin \emph{cognoscere} 'to get to know' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el conocimiento}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el conocimiento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el conocimiento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to assess, then the Spanish for the assessment, then say \emph{el conocimiento} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el conocimiento mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The knowledge\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la habilidad]{la habilidad — the skill, the ability}

\label{lesson:ES-C598-habilidad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the assessment, then the Spanish for the knowledge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la habilidad}
\textbf{la habilidad} — \textquotedblleft{}the skill, the ability\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tiene mucha habilidad con las manos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He is very skilful with his hands.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Habilidades sociales} — social skills.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{habilidad} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{habilitas} 'aptness', built on \emph{habilis} 'handy, fit', from \emph{habere} 'to hold' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la habilidad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la habilidad}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the assessment, then the Spanish for the knowledge, then say \emph{la habilidad} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la habilidad mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The skill, the ability\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la capacidad]{la capacidad — the ability, the capacity}

\label{lesson:ES-C598-capacidad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the knowledge, then the Spanish for the skill.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la capacidad}
\textbf{la capacidad} — \textquotedblleft{}the ability, the capacity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tiene capacidad para dirigir.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She has the ability to lead.}
\end{quote}

Also how much a place holds: \emph{capacidad para cien personas}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{capacidad} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{capacitas} 'room, capacity', built on \emph{capax} 'able to hold', from \emph{capere} 'to take' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la capacidad}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la capacidad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la capacidad}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the knowledge, then the Spanish for the skill, then say \emph{la capacidad} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la capacidad mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The ability, the capacity\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[esforzarse]{esforzarse — to make an effort, to try hard}

\label{lesson:ES-C598-esforzarse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the skill, then the Spanish for the ability.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: esforzarse}
\textbf{esforzarse} — \textquotedblleft{}to make an effort, to try hard\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Me esfuerzo mucho en clase.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I try very hard in class.}
\end{quote}

Stem change o$\to$ue: \emph{me esfuerzo}. Spelling: \emph{me esforcé}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{esforzarse} is built on \emph{fuerza} 'strength', inherited from Late Latin \emph{fortia}, from \emph{fortis} 'strong' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{esforzarse}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{esforzarse}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the skill, then the Spanish for the ability, then say \emph{esforzarse} again

\section[aportar]{aportar — to contribute, to bring}

\label{lesson:ES-C598-aportar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the ability, then the Spanish for to make an effort.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: aportar}
\textbf{aportar} — \textquotedblleft{}to contribute, to bring\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Cada persona aporta algo al equipo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Each person brings something to the team.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Aportar ideas} — to contribute ideas. \emph{La aportación} — the contribution.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{aportar} is inherited from Latin \emph{apportare} 'to carry to, to bring', built from \emph{ad} and \emph{portare} 'to carry' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aportar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aportar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{aportar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the ability, then the Spanish for to make an effort, then say \emph{aportar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
